items.before:
A modification is valued at its absolute value, so this deductive modification is a $5,600,000 action - not negative, not zero, and not the $64 million contract behind it.

$5,600,000 is above the $5M Class II tier. The SaP rung is only for commercial products and commercial services acquired under simplified procedures, and this is non-commercial work, so the smallest tier that reaches the action is $10M, which is Class III.

Board point: a descoping modification can feel like it needs less authority, but the policy measures size, not direction.

Cite: Army Warranting Program Policy v12 para 4.2 (absolute value of a modification) and Table 1; RFO FAR 12.201-1 and 12.001(c) (SaP, commercial only, $9,000,000).
items.after:
A modification is valued at its absolute value, so this deductive modification is a $5,600,000 action - not negative and not zero.

$5,600,000 is above the $5M Class II tier. The SaP rung is only for commercial products and commercial services acquired under simplified procedures, and this is non-commercial work, so the smallest tier that reaches the action is $10M, which is Class III.

Board point: a descoping modification can feel like it needs less authority, but the policy measures size, not direction.

Caution: the Policy v12 Summary of Key Changes entry for para 4.2 says that for a modification the warrant must be equal to or greater than the cumulative value of the contract including the modification. Read that way, this action is $64,000,000 plus $5,600,000, or $69,600,000 - still Class III, but at the $100M tier. Confirm which reading your office applies with the Chief, C&P.

Cite: Army Warranting Program Policy v12 para 4.2 (absolute value of a modification), Summary of Key Changes, and Table 1; RFO FAR 12.201-1 and 12.001(c) (SaP, commercial only, $9,000,000).
items.source: value_number $5,600,000 (absolute value of the modification, as TL01-TL40 count it) and Class III (non-commercial, so no SaP rung) confirmed. The explanation said the value is 'not the $64 million contract behind it', which the policy's own summary contradicts; a caution was added showing the class holds on that reading too ($64,000,000 + $5,600,000 = $69,600,000, Class III, $100M tier). Policy v12 Summary of Key Changes, entry for 4.2 (content/sources/army_warranting_policy_v12_mar2026.txt line 21): 'when determining the warrant level for a modification, it must be equal to or greater than the cumulative value of the contract including the modification'; para 4.2 body (line 77): 'include the base value, all options, any anticipated or actual ceiling values, plus the absolute value of a modification'.

items.before:
Para 4.2 values a modification at its absolute value. The absolute value of minus $410,000 is $410,000.

That is above the SAT of $350,000, so a Class I warrant cannot sign this reduction. The $500K tier of a Class II warrant covers it.

Board point: a price reduction is not a pass for a smaller warrant. Sign is irrelevant; size is not.

Cite: Army Warranting Program Policy v12 para 4.2 (absolute value of a modification) and Table 1.

unverifiable: Army Warranting Program Policy v12 is internally inconsistent on valuing a modification. Para 4.2 body: 'include the base value, all options, any anticipated or actual ceiling values, plus the absolute value of a modification'. Summary of Key Changes entry for 4.2: 'when determining the warrant level for a modification, it must be equal to or greater than the cumulative value of the contract including the modification'. TL63 and TL64 keep the modification-only value used by TL01-TL40 (their class is the same on either reading) and now carry a caution. Out of scope and NOT changed, but their class flips on the cumulative reading: TL06 ($4,900,200: I to II), TL20 ($42,300,000: II to III), TL33 ($250,000,000: I to IV). TL17 stays Class III ($36,200,000, $50M tier); TL21 cannot be recomputed because it gives no contract value. The practice cards in src/arcade/js/games/threshold-run.js also value a modification alone. Needs an owner decision or confirmation from DASA(P) policy staff or the Chief, C&P.
